practice.name: Clinic of the Cracked Cup
practice.address: Brisbane CBD (boutique rooms a short walk from Central Station; street address not published)

personal.philosophy_of_care: Built on kintsugi and wabi-sabi: cracks and struggles, repaired with care and insight, become the strongest parts of a person's story. A refuge for over-functioning helpers rather than a place for polished surfaces; no pressure to be fine, no gold stars for soldiering on.
personal.communication_approach: Creativity, warmth, a quirky personality and irreverent dark humour; spaces where people can put down their armour and piece themselves back together. Written in the first person on the practice site.
personal.lived_experience: Co-founded a lived-experience, neuro-affirming workplace; describes herself as a cracked cup in a cracked system.
personal.outside_medicine: Mother of two teenagers, a python called Penelope and an Italian Greyhound called Noodle; novelist and artist; self-described good-trouble maker and systems disruptor who champions the underdog.

quotes.text: She is a mother of two spirited teenagers, a python called Penelope, and an avant garde Italian Greyhound called Noodle.
In her spare time, she is also a novelist, an artist of all trades and master of few, the unapologetic owner of many doom piles, and a devoted nature and animal lover.
My therapeutic approach draws on something I call mental kintsugi. The art of repairing emotional cracks with compassion and meaning instead of shame or silence.
If you are over it, undone, or just holding it together with caffeine and dark humour, you are welcome here.
There's no pressure to be fine. No gold stars for soldiering on. Just room to breathe, grieve, and slowly come back to life.
I work from the Japanese philosophy of wabi-sabi, which finds beauty in the worn, the imperfect, and the incomplete.
Healing doesn't mean hiding what hurt you. It means making peace with the shape it left behind.
You might feel like a cracked pot. I think that makes you magic.

She has worked in diverse settings, from acute hospital wards and prisons, to schools and long-stay treatment centres, and has sat with people in some of their most challenging and transformative moments.
She dabbles as an amateur foodie, a gardener, and a self-confessed culture vulture who finds joy in everything from live theatre to street art.
